r.통화: Trinidad and Tobago dollar · 1 TTD = 198 won
r.문화권·종교: Roughly equal African and Indian heritage · carnival and steelpan
r.경제 체제: Energy-export economy · natural gas and petrochemicals such as ammonia and methanol
r.주식시장 시가총액: $3.9 billion, 44% of GDP (2001, listed domestic companies)
r.Consumer price level: 57% of the US level (2025, World Bank, household consumption at purchasing power parity against the market exchange rate)
r.한국이 파는 것: Cars 49%, Steel products 16%, Trucks 9%, Coated steel sheet 7% (2025, share of value)
r.한국이 사는 것: Natural gas (LNG, LPG) 76%, Organic chemicals 22% (2025, share of value)
r.정치 구도: A parliamentary republic led by a prime minister, with a president elected by parliament. Two parties take turns in power: the People's National Movement, drawing much of its support from Afro-Trinidadians, and the United National Congress, backed largely by Indo-Trinidadians, so election results often mirror the country's ethnic makeup. In the April 2025 election the United National Congress won 26 of the 41 seats and took power. Tobago has its own assembly and self-government, and expanding that autonomy is a constant issue. Gun crime linked to drug trafficking has risen to the point that the government has declared a state of emergency.

t.why: It is a rare Caribbean country that built an industry on oil and gas, and it is among the world's top exporters of ammonia and methanol made from gas. But gas output has fallen since peaking around 2010, so bringing in gas from the Dragon field on the Venezuelan side of the sea border has become a major economic goal. US sanctions on Venezuela have seen the project's licence revoked and reissued more than once, and in February 2026 Trinidad received new US licences for oil and gas activities in Venezuela. When the government backed US strikes in 2025 on Venezuelan boats the US said were carrying drugs, Venezuela suspended its gas agreements and declared the prime minister persona non grata. That put it at odds with neighbors pushing to keep the Caribbean a zone of peace, and the US capture of Venezuela's president in January 2026 shook the country next door even further.
t.rel: Many migrants have arrived from Venezuela across the sea to the south, making it sensitive to events there. A Caribbean Community member, it works with neighboring islands, and its final appeals are still heard by the Privy Council in London.
t.korea: Diplomatic relations were established in 1985. Korea opened a mission in Port of Spain that same year and upgraded it to an embassy in 2009. Korea buys natural gas, methanol and ammonia and sells cars and steel. The Korean community is small, numbering only a few dozen. In 2025 the two countries marked 40 years of ties with a Korean cultural event in Trinidad.
t.know: It is unusual that former British colonies still have their final appeals heard by a court in London. Independence constitutions often kept colonial-era criminal laws protected, so changing those laws is itself a big event.
etext: It turns offshore gas into liquefied natural gas, ammonia and methanol for export. More than a century of oil production has left it with the best-equipped energy workforce and infrastructure in the Caribbean.
Banks and retailers with branches across the Caribbean are headquartered there, making it an economic center for neighboring islands.

Falling gas output leaves plants short of feedstock, and developing the gas fields on the Venezuelan side depends on US sanctions. There is little industry beyond energy, and complaints about a shortage of US dollars are long-standing.
